PASSO 1: war, hatte, konnte, musste, wol: STEP 1: good news: the German Präteritum looks a lot like the English simple past — machte/made, kaufte/bought, kam/came, trank/drank. STEP 2: the trap is in usage: in everyday SPEECH, Germans use the Präteritum mainly for war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, durfte; for other verbs they say the Perfekt («Sie ist nach Hause gegangen»), and forms like «Sie ging nach Hause» belong mostly to stories and written texts. STEP 3: and "was + -ing" has no German equivalent: "I was working" is simply «Ich arbeitete» or, in speech, «Ich habe gearbeitet».
I had a lot of work.

PASSO 1: «Präteritum» é outra forma do p: STEP 1: the «Präteritum» is the other past tense, used mostly in WRITING and in texts. STEP 2: with «sein» and «haben», CONVERSATION also uses the Präteritum instead of the Perfekt: you say «Ich war müde» (I was tired), not «Ich bin müde gewesen»; you say «Ich hatte Fieber» (I had a fever), not «Ich habe Fieber gehabt». STEP 3: the forms of «sein»: ich war, du warst, er war, wir waren, ihr wart, sie waren. STEP 4: the forms of «haben»: ich hatte, du hattest, er hatte, wir hatten, ihr hattet, sie hatten. STEP 5: notice that «ich» and «er» are IDENTICAL (war, hatte), just like the modals in the present tense.

PASSO 1: os modais também usam o Präteri: STEP 1: the modals also use the Präteritum in conversation: «Ich konnte nicht kommen» (I couldn't come), «Ich musste arbeiten» (I had to work). STEP 2: the form is stem + «-te» + endings, and the UMLAUT DISAPPEARS: können → konnte; müssen → musste; dürfen → durfte; sollen → sollte; wollen → wollte. STEP 3: the endings: ich -te, du -test, er -te, wir -ten, ihr -tet, sie -ten («ich» and «er» are the same). STEP 4: the second verb stays in the INFINITIVE, at the end: «Ich wollte kommen, aber ich musste arbeiten.» STEP 5: learn the contrast «muss nicht» vs «darf nicht» — it's a classic trap for English speakers: «Du musst nicht kommen» = you don't have to come; «Du darfst nicht kommen» = you must not come (it's forbidden). "Must not" is «darf nicht», never «muss nicht».

PASSO 1: na CONVERSA, use o Perfekt para: STEP 1: in CONVERSATION, use the Perfekt for almost every verb and the Präteritum for «sein», «haben» and the modals. STEP 2: in TEXTS (news, stories, books), almost all verbs appear in the Präteritum. At this level you only need to RECOGNIZE these forms, not produce them. STEP 3: the most common forms are strong and irregular — and many look like their English cousins: gehen → ging (went); kommen → kam (came); sehen → sah (saw); fahren → fuhr; essen → aß (ate); trinken → trank (drank); schreiben → schrieb (wrote); lesen → las; sprechen → sprach (spoke); nehmen → nahm; geben → gab (gave); finden → fand (found). STEP 4: regular verbs use stem + «-te», the German version of "-ed": machen → machte; spielen → spielte (played); kaufen → kaufte.
